numberItems.stem: A child is standing 20 feet in front of the school bus bumper. Is the child in a danger zone?
options: No, the front danger zone ends at 12 feet
Yes, the front danger zone can reach 30 feet
No, the front danger zone ends at 10 feet
numberItems.explanation: The danger zone in front of the bus can reach 30 feet from the bumper; the first 12 feet is the most dangerous part, not the end of the zone (p. 10-1).

numberItems.stem: Which stretch in front of a school bus is the most dangerous?
options: The first 10 feet from the bumper
The first 12 feet from the bumper
The area from 12 to 30 feet out
numberItems.explanation: The front danger zone reaches up to 30 feet, and the first 12 feet in front of the bumper is the most dangerous part (p. 10-1).

numberItems.stem: How far behind the rear bumper of a school bus does the danger zone reach?
numberItems.explanation: The danger zone reaches 12 feet behind the rear bumper, the same as each side; 30 feet is the front limit (p. 10-1).

numberItems.stem: [CA] A parent group charters a bus that has seat belts. Which children may the group not put on the bus unless they are buckled?
numberItems.explanation: Parents, guardians and chartering parties may not put a child at least 8 but under 16 on the bus unless properly buckled; since July 1, 2018 every passenger on a bus with belts must be belted, with exceptions (p. 10-1).

numberItems.stem: Your outside flat mirror shows the road only 100 feet behind the bus. What should you do?
options: Have it adjusted so it shows 200 feet, or 4 bus lengths, behind the bus
Have it adjusted so it shows 400 feet behind the bus
numberItems.explanation: Flat mirrors should show 200 feet, or 4 bus lengths, behind the bus; 400 feet is how far the blind spot behind the bus can reach (p. 10-2).

numberItems.stem: On most school buses, about how far back does the blind spot directly behind the rear bumper run?
numberItems.explanation: The blind spot behind the rear bumper runs 50 to 150 feet and can reach 400 feet on a long, wide bus; 200 feet is what the flat mirrors should show (p. 10-2).

numberItems.stem: How much of the road beside the bus should each outside convex mirror show?
options: At least 1 traffic lane on each side
200 feet, or 4 bus lengths, behind the bus
numberItems.explanation: Convex mirrors should show the entire side up to the mirror mounts, the front of the rear tires, and at least 1 traffic lane on each side; 200 feet is the flat mirror view (p. 10-2).

numberItems.stem: The overhead inside mirror has a large blind spot that starts at the rear bumper. How far behind the bus can it reach?
numberItems.explanation: The overhead mirror's blind spot starts at the rear bumper and can reach 400 feet or more; use the outside side mirrors to watch traffic there (p. 10-3).

numberItems.stem: About how many seconds before a stop should you turn on the alternating flashing amber lights?
options: Only after the bus has stopped
numberItems.explanation: Amber lights go on at least 200 feet or about 5–10 seconds before the stop; 3–5 seconds is the right turn signal timing, and red lights are the ones used once stopped (p. 10-4).

numberItems.stem: About how many seconds before pulling over at a stop should you turn on the right turn signal?
options: Only once the bus has stopped
numberItems.explanation: Turn on the right turn signal about 100–300 feet or about 3–5 seconds before pulling over; 5–10 seconds is the amber light timing (p. 10-4).

numberItems.stem: Why should you stop with the front bumper at least 10 feet from the students waiting at a stop?
options: So passing cars have room to get by
So the students must walk to the bus and you can see them move
So the stop arm has room to swing out
numberItems.explanation: Stopping at least 10 feet away makes the students walk to the bus, so you can see them move (p. 10-4).

numberItems.stem: After students get off on the route, how far from the side of the bus should they walk?
options: At least 10 feet, to where you can plainly see them
At least 30 feet, to the far corner
They should wait right beside the door until the bus leaves
numberItems.explanation: Students walk at least 10 feet away from the side of the bus, to a spot where the driver can plainly see all of them (p. 10-5).

numberItems.stem: [CA] Where no officer or traffic signal controls traffic, up to what grade must the driver escort students who cross the road?
numberItems.explanation: The driver must escort prekindergarten, kindergarten, and grades 1 through 8 across the road, using an approved hand-held STOP sign (p. 10-5).

numberItems.stem: During the 7 pull-away steps on the route, which signal do you turn on?
numberItems.explanation: The route pull-away steps are: close the door, put it in gear, release the parking brake, turn off the red lights, turn on the left turn signal, check all mirrors, and let heavy traffic clear (p. 10-4).

numberItems.stem: Pulling away after unloading at school takes 9 steps. Which 2 steps are added to the 7 route steps?
options: Fasten your safety belt and start the engine
Count the students and sound the horn
Turn on the amber lights and open the door
numberItems.explanation: Because the engine was off at school, the pull-away adds fastening your safety belt and starting the engine to the route steps (p. 10-6).
